batchName: Empire: Claudius and Nero (AD 41-68) - Hard Batch 1

questions.question: What happened to the leading British war chief captured in AD 50?
options: He was made governor of the new province
He was exiled to an island in the Tiber
He was sent to fight as a gladiator
He was paraded in a triumph and strangled
Claudius spared him, and he lived on land provided by Rome
questions.explanation: Claudius spared him, a rare mercy for a defeated enemy. The conquest nonetheless left resentment that exploded under Nero.
questions.sourceQuote: When a leading British war chief was captured in AD 50, Claudius spared him, and he lived out his life on land provided by Rome, a rare mercy for a defeated enemy.

questions.question: Why do some modern historians doubt that Agrippina murdered Claudius? (select all that apply)
options: Agrippina was away at Antium when he died
His food taster kept his job under Nero
A doctor's report recorded natural causes
AD 54 was an unhealthy year in Rome
questions.explanation: Claudius's serious illness, the food taster keeping his job and an unhealthy year all cast doubt on the murder story. Ancient writers said her motive was Claudius talking about his own son coming of age.
questions.sourceQuote: Claudius had been seriously ill, his food taster kept his job under Nero, and AD 54 was an unhealthy year in Rome.

questions.question: How did the Roman governor defeat Boudica's far larger army?
options: Luring them onto ships off Anglesey
Javelins and a wedge charge from a narrow pass
Starving the rebels in a long siege
Bribing neighbouring tribes to desert her
questions.explanation: With almost 10,000 men in a narrow pass backed by woods, the Romans hurled javelins and charged in wedge formation. Boudica died soon after, by poison or illness depending on the source.
questions.sourceQuote: Heavily outnumbered, the Romans hurled javelins, charged in wedge formation and crushed the Britons.

questions.question: Claudius's census of AD 48 counted about how many adult male citizens?
questions.explanation: The census counted 5,984,072 adult male citizens, about a million more than a generation before.
questions.sourceQuote: His census of AD 48 counted 5,984,072 adult male citizens, about a million more than a generation before.

questions.question: Why do modern historians doubt Tacitus's claim that Nero's mistress drove him to kill his mother?
options: Nero was in Greece at the time
He married her only three years later
She had been dead for two years
She later accused Nero's tutor instead
Agrippina had approved of the affair
questions.explanation: If she had pushed him to remove his mother, a quick marriage might be expected; instead he waited three years. Tacitus's Annals give the fullest account of Nero.
questions.sourceQuote: Modern historians doubt this, since he married her only three years later.

questions.question: What did Nero do for Rome's people after returning during the Great Fire? (select all that apply)
options: Paid to clear bodies and rubble
Opened his palaces to the homeless
Cancelled all debts for a year
questions.explanation: Nero paid for clearing bodies and rubble, opened his palaces to the homeless and brought in food. Far from cutting taxes, he later raised them to pay for rebuilding.
questions.sourceQuote: Nero returned, paid to clear bodies and rubble, opened his palaces to the homeless and brought in food.

questions.question: Roughly how long after Nero's death did the Greek senator, one of the three main sources, write?
questions.explanation: The Greek senator wrote more than 150 years after Nero's death, while Tacitus and the biographer wrote more than fifty years after. All three usually took the Senate's side.
questions.sourceQuote: Tacitus and the biographer wrote more than fifty years after Nero's death, the Greek senator more than 150.

questions.question: At least how many impostors claimed to be Nero after his death?
questions.explanation: In the eastern provinces many believed he would return, and at least three impostors appeared. His death ended his dynasty and led to civil war.
questions.sourceQuote: In the eastern provinces many believed he would return, and at least three impostors claimed to be Nero.

questions.question: How did Claudius deal with those involved in his nephew's murder?
options: Pardoned most but executed the actual assassins
Had the Senate try and acquit the assassins
Exiled the senators and spared the guards
Executed every guardsman and senator involved
questions.explanation: He pardoned most people involved but executed the actual killers, partly for his own safety. The assassins had also murdered his nephew's wife and daughter.
questions.sourceQuote: Claudius pardoned most people involved but executed the actual assassins, partly for his own safety.

questions.question: In AD 37 Claudius finally held a top office for the first time. What was it?
options: Praetor in charge of Rome's courts
Chief priest of the Etruscan cults
Consul, alongside his nephew the emperor
questions.explanation: He served as consul with his nephew, the reigning emperor, who mocked and humiliated him. He revived the censorship only later, in AD 47, as emperor.
questions.sourceQuote: Only in AD 37 did he hold a top office, serving as consul (*consul*), one of the two highest magistrates, alongside his nephew, the reigning emperor, who mocked and humiliated him.
